title: U.S. House · California's 43rd District
area: South Los Angeles and surrounding communities including Inglewood, Compton, Gardena and Hawthorne, redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Maxine Waters (D) and Republican Cristian Morales advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating two other Democratic candidates.

candidates.name: Maxine Waters
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 43rd District (since 2013); previously represented predecessor districts since 1991

summary.text: Maxine Waters is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in California's 43rd District. A former Head Start teacher and volunteer coordinator, she served in the California State Assembly from 1977 to 1991 and in the U.S. House since 1991, including as chair of the House Financial Services Committee from 2019 to 2022. Her official biography emphasizes her work on housing, financial services, health care and international debt relief.

background.text: Born in St. Louis, Missouri, in 1938. According to her official biography, she was the fifth of 13 children raised by a single mother and began working at age 13 in factories and restaurants.

After moving to Los Angeles she worked in garment factories and at the telephone company, and attended California State University, Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree (in sociology, 1970, per Ballotpedia).
Began her public-service career as a teacher and volunteer coordinator in the Head Start program.

Served in the California State Assembly (District 48) from 1977 to 1991, rising to Democratic Caucus Chair; her official biography cites state legislation on divestment of state pension funds from South Africa, a plant-closure law and a statewide child abuse prevention training program from that period.

Has served on the Democratic National Committee since 1980, according to her official biography, and was a leader in five presidential campaigns (Kennedy 1980, Jackson 1984 and 1988, Clinton 1992 and 1996).
Elected to the U.S. House in 1990 and took office in 1991, representing California's 29th District (1991-1993), the 35th District (1993-2013) and the 43rd District (2013-present).
Became the first woman and first African American to chair the House Financial Services Committee (chair 2019-2022; ranking member 2023-2024; committee member in the 2025-2026 term, per Ballotpedia).

Founded Community Build after the 1992 Los Angeles civil unrest and, in the 1980s, Project Build; co-founded the Black Women's Forum. She is a founding member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and a past chair of the Congressional Black Caucus, according to her official biography.
Her official biography states she is married to Sidney Williams, a former U.S. Ambassador to the Bahamas, and has two adult children and two grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says she remains committed to expanding and reforming the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program so tenants do not lose housing assistance due to budget shortfalls.
Says she remains committed to supporting initiatives that reduce health disparities and ensure equitable care for all.

positions.summary: Condemned the Trump administration's efforts to target sanctuary cities and expand its mass deportation agenda.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the following statement condemning Donald Trump and his Administration's efforts to weaponize federal resources and government authority to target sanctuary cities and expand his mass deportation agenda, including reported proposals that could disrupt operations at major airports like Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

positions.summary: In an October 2018 press statement, opposed Republican proposals to cut Medicare and Medicaid, describing them as programs that provide affordable health care.
positions.quote: Medicare and Medicaid save lives, help people live longer, and provide the peace of mind that comes with affordable health care that is there when you need it.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services for the 2025-2026 term; chaired the committee from 2019 to 2023 and served as ranking member from 2023 to 2025.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website statements or Candidate Connection survey responses were found. Positions above are drawn from her official House issues pages; her health-care, immigration and criminal-justice issue pages otherwise consist of press-release listings without further statements matching the fixed issue set (e.g. no direct statement on abortion, guns, or police funding was found).

candidates.name: Cristian Morales
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating two Democratic candidates.

summary.text: Cristian Morales is the Republican candidate in California's 43rd District. Born in Guatemala, he describes a 20-plus-year career in manufacturing leadership, most recently as a director of operations. He ran for California governor in 2022 (a first campaign for office) and is running now on a campaign slogan of "ForAllVoices," according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

background.text: Born in Guatemala City, Guatemala; his family immigrated to the United States during the 1970s, according to his Candidate Connection survey.
Graduated from West Lafayette High School (Indiana), per Ballotpedia.

Earned a bachelor's degree in management from Purdue University in 2002, a graduate degree from Indiana University in 2007, and a graduate degree in industrial and labor relations from Cornell University in 2008.

Describes a 20-plus-year career in manufacturing (automotive, aerospace and defense) leading multicultural teams; Ballotpedia lists his profession as business executive and career as a director of operations.

Ran as a Republican for California governor in 2022, describing it as his first venture into politics; he received 25,086 votes in the June top-two primary and did not advance to the general election.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary to the November general election for the 43rd District, which his survey says includes Compton, Watts, Hawthorne, Inglewood, Gardena, Lawndale and Torrance.

priorities.text: Immigration, eradicating generational poverty, and protecting constitutional rights and equal opportunity (his listed policy areas).

candidates.researchNotes: 2026 Ballotpedia survey gives general themes only. NBC Los Angeles reports his campaign website supports tax cuts and reduced spending, but the site itself was not located, so that is not cited. Earlier 2022 gubernatorial statements not used.
